record.one_liner: Relationship-focused CRM built for Google Workspace, offering pipeline, contact, and lead management.
record.auth_notes: API keys are generated self-serve in Copper's web app (System settings > API Keys) and sent in request headers with the generating user's email. OAuth2.0 authorization-code grant is described as the preferred method for partner/third-party integrations, but registering an OAuth app requires obtaining client_id/client_secret from Copper (documentation points developers to contact Copper's partnerships team), so OAuth app creation is not purely self-serve.
record.access_notes: Copper's own pricing page lists 'API & Embedded integration SDK' as a feature included only in the Professional and Business plan tiers, not the lower Basic/Starter tiers. API key generation (System settings > API Keys) is otherwise self-serve for users on a qualifying paid plan.
record.api_breadth_basis: developer.copper.com documents CRUD/bulk operations across many distinct resource families: Account & Users, Leads, People, Companies, Opportunities, Projects, Tasks, Activities, Custom Fields, Tags, File Upload (S3-based), Webhooks, and Related Items — well beyond the ~15-endpoint narrow threshold.
record.blocker_notes: A working toolkit requires a Copper account on the Professional plan ($59/seat/mo, per third-party pricing summaries) or Business plan, since API access is gated out of the cheaper tiers per Copper's own pricing page. Once on a qualifying plan, API key auth is immediate/self-serve; OAuth app registration additionally requires contacting Copper's partnerships team.
